subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Orion Medical
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@orionmed.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionmed.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Orion Medical

Hi Sara / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Appreciate you confirming any gaps.

Key pain points & goals
- Predictable latency for conversational workflows (primary use case: triage chat for clinicians). Target p99 < 200ms for short responses (~64 tokens).
- Strict data isolation and auditability: patient PHI must never leave Orion network; need VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for key control.
- Predictable cost and throughput for 24/7 production traffic with daily peaks during morning rounds.
- Ability to scale quickly for product demos and heavier batch jobs (nightly summarization).

Proposed Dedicated capacity profile (high level)
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPU slots for 24/7, with burst pool of 6 GPUs for peak windows (total reserved 10, burst as needed).
- Multi-tenant isolation: Dedicated GPU pool with network isolation (VPC), disk encryption, and separated S3 buckets per environment.
- Autoscaling policy: target latency SLO, scale up to burst pool on queue depth; warm KV cache retention for interactive workloads.
- SLA targets: 99.95% uptime for the dedicated cluster, p99 inference latency < 200ms for small-context calls; SLO-based alerting to Orion ops.

Compliance & integration needs
- SOC 2 + audit logs for all inference requests (we provide request-level tracing and export).
- Customer-managed KMS (we support AWS KMS & Google KMS).
- Option: on-prem deployment if required for PHI (we discussed Private deployment; will scope separately).

Next steps
1) We will send an SOW + committed quote (attached) by EOD Friday.
2) Technical deep-dive with Vivek (solutions) to validate VPC/KMS/networking — proposed slot: Mon May 24 10:00–11:00 PT.
3) Daniel / procurement to share PO timeline and any standard contract redlines.
4) Pilot option: 30-day pilot on reduced committed capacity (we can scope) if you want to validate latency/cost before full commit.

Attachments: Orion_DCAP_SOW_v2.pdf, redwood-dedicated-quote-20270522.xlsx

If anything above needs correction, flag it here and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll schedule the deep-dive and route the SOW for signatures.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@orionmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionmed.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 19:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Orion Medical

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The PHI requirement is firm; we will need customer-managed KMS and the VPC peering model (not a shared subnet).
- For the SLA targets, can you confirm whether the p99 <200ms includes network transit to our VPC or only inference time inside the cluster?
- Procurement timeline: we aim to have a PO in 2–3 weeks pending legal review. Daniel will be the primary contact for the PO.
- Pilot: interested in the 30-day pilot to validate latency before full commit. Can the pilot be limited to 2 A100-equivalent GPUs with monitoring access?

Can you also confirm what support hours are included (business hours vs 24/7 for on-call escalation)?

Happy to proceed with the proposed Mon May 24 deep-dive — Daniel, can you make that slot?

Best,
Sara Jenkins
CTO, Orion Medical
sara.jenkins@orionmed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@orionmed.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionmed.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Orion Medical — technical checklist before deep-dive

Vivek / Rishi — quick internal note ahead of Mon’s deep-dive. Sara flagged a couple of items we should prepare: 

Tech checklist (to bring to the call)
- Confirm exact network model: VPC peering details, IP allowlist, required CIDR ranges, and whether Orion requires private subnets only.
- KMS flow: outline of customer-managed KMS key creation, rotation, and how we store key IDs; note any constraints for GCP vs AWS.
- Pilot scope: we should be ready to propose a 30-day pilot on 2 A100-equivalent GPUs with telemetry dashboard access and sample SLA reporting.
- Latency SLA definition: define what counts toward p99 (inference-only vs end-to-end). Recommend we propose both numbers and call out network variability.
- Deployment options: confirm VPC-only (hosted dedicated) vs Private (on-prem) lift-and-shift steps if they request full on-prem.

Deliverables before Mon:
- One-pager network & KMS flow (I’ll attach draft).
- Updated SOW and committed quote (attached to thread).

I’ll run the deep-dive meeting; Vivek, can you take the networking/KMS section? Rishi, pls have a note on autoscaling behavior for the Dedicated fleet.

-Marissa

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orionmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@orionmed.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Orion Medical

Marissa / Sara — confirmed, thanks for the clear recap. A couple of procurement items from my side: 

- We should receive the SOW + official quote by EOD Friday so legal can start reviewing. Please include a DocuSign-ready contract (we use a standard PO + signature flow).
- Pilot: Daniel confirms we want to run the 30-day pilot on 2 A100-equivalent GPUs. Please include pilot pricing and a short checklist of what telemetry we get access to.
- Support: we’ll need a 24/7 on-call escalation for production incidents (during pilot we can do business hours, but committed deployment needs 24/7 coverage).
- Timeline: assuming no major redlines, procurement aims to sign within 3 weeks. If you need earlier commitment for capacity, flag now.

Next steps for Redwood: DocuSign link, finalized SOW, and pilot order form.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Manager, Procurement | Orion Medical
